full_judgment: 18. Furthermore, it suffices to note that the inability of any entity to meet its obligations presupposes a state of incapacity or insolvency of that entity. That presumption, this Court finds, cannot readily be made in this particular case given the information and material brought on record on behalf of the Respondent No. 1 attesting to its status as a solvent and viable entity. In these facts and circumstances, this Court is satisfied overall that the Respondent No. 1 has been able to formulate a credible and duly substantiated defense against the liability under the Guarantees and that such defense has been raised bona fide and is not to be treated as a cloak to evade payment due to the Petitioner. It is this Court's view that any insistence on the part of the Petitioner for the Respondent No. 1 to be wound up in such circumstances would amount to these proceedings being abused by way of a coercive tactic for realization of money.
